bug_semantics: js_mapped_arguments_mark walks a mapped-arguments fast array of JSVarRef pointers and calls mark_func (during JS_RunGC this is gc_decref_child) on every non-null entry without testing is_detached. Captured/non-detached JSVarRefs created by get_var_ref are not add_gc_object'd and leave list_head link.prev/link.next uninitialized. gc_decref_child then list_del's those links, turning attacker-controlled heap reuse of a JSVarRef into a write-what-where (prev->next = next) and possible native code execution. Trigger is a non-strict mapped arguments object plus GC (qjs -C): function f(a){ arguments; gc(); } f(0). NVD CWE-94 is a mis-tag; the defect is uninitialized GC-list pointers, not code generation.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable mark loop was first written in this repo by c27cdfc43d5e33b92566d327e00e0e4ebaa207c3 (Port arguments object optimizations, PR #1315), which added js_mapped_arguments_mark and wired it as the JS_CLASS_MAPPED_ARGUMENTS GC mark callback. The same commit stores mapped-argument elements as JSVarRef* in fast-array mode and creates those refs via get_var_ref, which still returns non-detached stack-capturing JSVarRefs whose GC header links are never initialized. The function body at the BIC is if (var_refs[i]) mark_func(rt, &var_refs[i]->header); with no is_detached guard. That body is absent in parent cb83fd9 (JS_CLASS_MAPPED_ARGUMENTS had NULL mark/finalizer) and is blamed unchanged through pre-fix dcfa6c1. The commit message cites bellard/quickjs@9f11034 (full 9f11034a5a, arguments-object optimizations); that is an upstream reference, not a prior write in this history. PR #1315 landed as individual commits rather than a squash, so c27cdfc is the smallest surviving first-write.

reasoning: CVE-2026-37630 is a published MITRE record pointing at issue #1400; the GitHub advisory is not withdrawn. The vendor accepted it as a real GC memory-safety bug and merged PR #1401. The attack path is: non-strict mapped arguments object (fast array of JSVarRef*) -> js_mapped_arguments_mark during JS_RunGC -> mark_func/gc_decref_child on a non-detached JSVarRef whose list_head was never initialized -> list_del write-what-where. The smallest commit that first wrote those mark lines in this repository is c27cdfc43d5e33b92566d327e00e0e4ebaa207c3. git log -L/-S and pre-fix blame all stop at that commit; the immediate parent cb83fd9 lacks the function and used a NULL mapped-arguments mark callback, so this is not a move/refactor of existing NG code. It is a first-time port of Bellard arguments-object optimizations (ref 9f11034a5a) into quickjs-ng via PR #1315's individual 'Port arguments object optimizations' commit, not a squash of unrelated members and not a later backport of already-present lines. The same BIC also created the mapped-arguments var_refs via get_var_ref without putting non-detached refs on the GC list, so the flawed mark and the uninitialized-link objects were introduced together. The fix 3973106 is the direct one-line is_detached guard plus regression tests; it is in v0.13.0 and not in the advisory's v0.12.1. AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object: human maintainer identity, no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot markers. Therefore the real vulnerability has human authorship (NOT_AI).
